title: import: a lookup cell that names the record by the target object's title field answers reference_not_found — resolveRef never reads nameField, and a formula title is not matchable
body:
Ruled: 6308445871 · letter A · 2026-10-21T05:00Z

**Filing gate ①: a public door that refuses its own documented key, measured, with a named location.** `finding` class a. **Reader who acts:** the `domain:engine` seat (`packages/core`, per SKILL.md's lane table), in one PR. Filed by `domain:cli` seat 2 (`os-justin`, `session_01LmjU2x1faLZ39DVTFyVca6`, seat post #22648), from #24944's dev report `6301167497` (PR #24980, out-of-scope finding 1, and its open question). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Measured (PR #24980's fixture, through `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import`)

| Lookup cell | Target's title | Answer |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `John Smith` | `nameField: 'full_name'`, a formula | `reference_not_found` |
| `Wren` | `displayNameField: 'nickname'`, stored | `reference_not_found` |
| `Acme (EMEA)` | `nameField: 'display_title'`, a formula | `reference_not_found` |

On `main`, the cells `VP of Engineering`, `Chief Procurement Officer` and `Acme` resolved, by the job `title` and by `name`. Those matched by an unrelated column, and they fail as ambiguous as soon as two contacts share a title.

## Where

- `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` `resolveRef` (about `:682`) tries:
  - the id;
  - the lookup's own `displayField`;
  - a fixed list (`name`, `title`, `label`, `full_name`, `email`, `username`).
- It never reads the target object's declared title field: `@objectstack/spec/data` `resolveDisplayField`, ADR-0079.
- `full_name` is on the list, yet `John Smith` still misses. A formula title is not matchable by a `where` filter there.

## Why it matters now

PR #24980 (#24944, the p1 the maintainer's HotCRM 18.0 round found) makes the list export write each lookup cell by the target's declared title. The export was writing a contact's job title. So a file the export writes no longer re-imports a lookup column whose target title is a formula or is not on the import's key list. The `domain:cli` seat landed the export fix first, because:
- the export cell is the defect the maintainer measured;
- the old round trip matched by an unrelated column;
- the import failure is a loud `reference_not_found`, not a silent wrong link.

## Wanted

- `resolveRef` resolves a lookup cell by the target object's title field, with the same single rule (`resolveDisplayField`), after the id and the lookup's own `displayField`.
- A formula title is matched by the engine's own record-title resolution, not by a `where` on a column that does not exist.
- An ambiguous title (two records share it) answers its own refusal, as the import's other ambiguous matches do. It never links the first hit.
- Read-side checks stay as they are (#22739: no match against a target whose exposure refuses reads).

## Neighbours

- #24944 / PR #24980 (the export side).
- Closed: #22785 and #22739 (other import reference refusals).
- The export's own header names a re-import contract for date cells only. No round-trip contract for lookup cells is declared.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues`, objectstack, open and closed: "import reference_not_found lookup nameField title field resolveRef export re-import round trip", 10 hits. None names the import side of the title rule.

Dedupe words: import reference_not_found nameField; resolveRef title field; export re-import lookup round trip; import-runner formula title.
